name: Haiku macro/sector rotation
strategy: Quality defensive rate-beneficiary positioning: emphasize yield-oriented stocks and low-volatility factors resilient to post-FOMC volatility while capturing utilities and financial dividend yield.
reassessment_note: Round 3 is outperforming Round 2 (+0.60% vs -1.80%) on defensive quality positioning. To maintain diversification per novelty rule (< 50% overlap with R2), rebalance to emphasize orthogonal factors: increase utilities (XLU 3%→14%) as rising-rate dividend-yield safe haven, reduce emerging-market currency risk (EEM 13%→5%) given dollar-strength tailwind from rate hike, maintain low-vol quality factors (SPLV, USMV). Utilities historically support portfolios through rate-shock volatility while dividend yields become more competitive vs bonds. This creates macro-hedge positioning: R2 is aggressive rate-winner play, R3 is defensive quality diversifier.

positions.thesis: Healthcare sector core defensive holding in quality-focused portfolio. Earnings resilience independent of rate cycles; stable revenue from aging demographics and healthcare inflation. Lower beta to equity volatility. Dividend yield 2-3% supports quality income narrative. Maintains exposure to secular trends while providing downside cushion through reduced sensitivity to FOMC rate-shock volatility.

Utilities sector upgrade from 3% (major underweight) to 14% to capitalize on rising-rate dividend-yield appeal. Higher rates (3.75%-4.00% likely) make utility dividend yields (2.5%-4.5%+) increasingly attractive vs bond alternatives. Regulated utility cash flows are durable through rate shocks. Sector provides portfolio ballast through low equity-market correlation, stable earnings, and dividend growth potential. Defensive positioning orthogonal to R2's energy/financial aggression.

Financial sector quality exposure (lower than R2's 20% to maintain novelty) captures rate-hike net interest margin expansion while maintaining quality/dividend filter. Large financial names offer 2-3% dividend yields and earnings visibility. Positioned as quality equity exposure to rate beneficiary rather than aggressive carry trade. Balances dividend growth narrative with sector fundamentals.

S&P 500 Low Volatility ETF provides defensive quality-factor exposure uncorrelated to rate cycles. Selected low-vol names have demonstrated FOMC-shock resilience through volatility clustering. Diversified across sectors with bias to stable earnings and dividend-paying names. Lower beta to post-FOMC equity dislocation. Factor exposure that outperforms in uncertainty environments.

US Low Volatility large-cap quality factor positioning. Focuses on domestic blue-chip companies with stable earnings and low historical volatility. Dividend-weighted construction (avg yield 2%+) supports quality income strategy. Provides uncorrelated return stream vs rate-sensitive growth. Essential diversifier within quality defensive framework, protecting downside while maintaining equity participation.

Materials sector minimal allocation (6%) provides cyclical diversification without overcommitting to commodity-price risk. Maintains some exposure to structural growth in energy infrastructure (rare earths for wind/solar). Reduced weighting (vs prior 8%) reflects caution on growth slowdown in rate-hike scenario. Token position allows capture of any commodity-strength continuation without asymmetric downside if growth disappoints.

Emerging markets dramatic reduction (13%→5%) reflects currency headwind from Fed rate hike. Higher US rates strengthen dollar, creating FX drag on EM returns. Policy divergence (Fed tightening vs central bank easing) reduces relative attractiveness. Minimal 5% allocation maintains diversification and exposure to long-term EM growth narrative while limiting currency impact on returns. Tactical underweight vs historical allocation.
